open-question.question: Once the sweep writes lift, fold, remove, and commit into its own batched call, does it still follow the two shared answer procedures for anything (the lift step's no-recommendation guard, the answer core's analyse questions), or does its own file state every per-question step and the two procedures say they are followed by the single-question skills alone, as the recommendation pass's batching did in its own file?
open-question.alternative: The sweep's own file states every per-question mechanical step its batched call runs: lift with its silent skip, the fold through the fold command, remove with the lifted option, and the commit. It stops following answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md altogether and keeps a reference to answer-procedure.md only for the judgment that call cannot do: the analyse step's questions, in whatever form the sweep keeps them, and the fold step's rules on what the decision text says (clean prose, no citation marker, the live document's section names). The lift procedure's intro names only answer-open-question-with-recommendation. The core's intro is reworded to say the sweep follows its analyse step and fold-content rules, not its tool steps. The CLAUDE.md sweep invariant and the shell-literal clause are reworded to match. The split is the recommendation pass's own: that pass still follows the shared pick procedure for its judgment and keeps every write, lift, and commit in its own fixed call. The sweep likewise keeps one home for the decision-writing rules it shares with every answer path, while its file is the only place its mechanics are described. The core's intro has to state a partial-follower relationship, which a later editor must keep accurate step by step. How much of the analyse step is left to reference depends on the mooting-cascade and contradiction-advisory questions; if both drop that judgment, the reference shrinks to the fold-content rules alone.

The sweep keeps following answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md and answer-procedure.md once per question, and both procedures' text stays as it is, their "followed ... once per question, by the inline answer sweep" sentences included. The sweep's own file lists where its batched call departs from them: no per-question locate (the compact view stands in for it), the fold written through the fold command instead of a file edit, the lift guard's stop turned into the silent skip it already is, and lift, fold, remove, and commit run inside the one call instead of as separate steps. The CLAUDE.md sweep invariant keeps "following answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md from its lift step", and the shell-literal clause still covers "the per-question calls of the procedures it follows". Smallest change. The shared procedures, the single-question skills that follow them, and the invariants that cite them stay untouched, and the analyse questions and fold-content rules (clean prose, no citation marker, the live document's section names) keep one home. The sweep would "follow" procedures whose locate, fold mechanism, guard behaviour, and step order it overrides almost entirely. A runner reading them could then run a locate or an Edit fold that the batched call never makes, which is the drift the batch exists to remove, and a later edit to the procedures has to be checked against a list of exceptions held in a different file.

The sweep keeps following both procedures, and the procedures themselves are edited to describe the sweep's batched form beside the single-question form. The answer core's locate step gets an exception for a caller holding the compact view, its fold step names the fold command for the sweep while the single-question skills keep their Edit-based fold, and the lift procedure's guard states the sweep's silent skip. The sweep's file shows the call and points at the procedures for what each section does, and the CLAUDE.md invariants keep naming the procedures as the sweep's. Each per-question rule still lives in exactly one file. Someone reading the answer procedures sees every path that records an answer, the batched one included, and the fold-before-remove and option-passing rules cannot drift between the sweep and the single-question skills. It adds the branches CLAUDE.md rules out: the recording core is meant to stay "a pass-through recorder that gained one input and no branch", and its inputs-as-given contract is shared with the literal answer-open-question. Every single-question runner would also read sweep-only text it must ignore, and the procedures would describe a shell call whose full form lives only in the sweep's file.

As with "Core judgment only", the sweep's file states every mechanical step of its batched call. It also keeps following answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md, but only for the lift step's definitions: ANSWER is the lift's whole printed line, RECORDED OPTION is the text before the first spaced em dash, and both come from that print alone, never from an applied-principle or alternative (the provenance-free derivation). Like "Core judgment only", it follows answer-procedure.md for the analyse step and the fold-content rules. Both procedures' intros are reworded to say which of their parts the sweep follows. The CLAUDE.md wording "The lift lives in that procedure" stays true for the sweep as well. The derivation rule that keeps a recorded decision provenance-free stays in one file for both recommendation-recording paths, so the sweep and answer-open-question-with-recommendation cannot drift on what a lifted line yields. The sweep would reference a one-paragraph definition from a procedure whose other two parts (the stop-and-report guard and the wholesale delegation to the core) it overrides, so two procedures need step-level partial-follower wording instead of one. How the batched call gets its remove option value depends on the option-value-source question and may make the RECORDED OPTION definition moot for the sweep.

The sweep's own file states every per-question step: the mechanics of the batched call (lift and its silent skip, the fold through the fold command, remove with the lifted option, the commit, the stop after a fold) and whatever per-question judgment the sweep keeps. That includes the fold-content rules (clean prose, no citation marker, the live document's section names) and the ANSWER and option derivation from the lift's print. It follows neither answer procedure. Both procedures' intros say they are followed by the single-question skills alone, with no other change to their text. The CLAUDE.md sweep invariant drops "following answer-with-recommendation-procedure.md from its lift step", and the shell-literal clause drops its "per-question calls of the procedures it follows" wording. The sweep's file is a complete account of what a run does, with no cross-file exception list. The shared procedures go back to describing one question recorded by hand-paced steps, with no batched reader to keep in mind, which matches the goal's split that only the sweep uses the fold command. The rules for decision text and option derivation now exist in two places, answer-procedure.md for the three single-question skills and the sweep's file for the sweep. A later change to how a decision is worded or where it lands has to be made twice or the paths drift. How much judgment the sweep's file has to restate depends on the mooting-cascade and contradiction-advisory questions.

open-question.question: The compact view gives the sweep each walked question's id, question text, and lifted pick, that is the option id and the recommendation's one-line rationale, and the whole XML is no longer read, while today's folds draw the recorded decision's detail from the picked alternative's what-it-is text. Is each sweep decision written from the lifted line alone, or does the compact view also carry the picked alternative's what-it-is text for every walked id?

The goal keeps the whole read of requirements.md beside the compact view, but the compact view's fixed call covers the question document only. Is requirements.md read with the file-reading tool as a separate step, as today, or is that read written into the same fixed shell call so the sweep's setup is one call?

A stop after a fold leaves a decision folded into requirements.md but uncommitted, and the sweep is re-run from the top after a fix, with no clean-tree precondition today. Does the batched sweep check that its two files are clean before recording anything and stop on a dirty one, or does it run regardless, letting a stranded fold ride into the first answer's commit?

When the review pass's new Decisions consistency step finds two recorded decisions in conflict, does it author an open-question block asking which entry stands, committed with the pass like any other new gap, or only flag the pair in the pass's report beside the still-open list?

The batched-call test extracts the fixed call from a rendered sweep file and fills its per-question placeholders, but nothing yet says how the test finds the call and its repeating per-question section. By what anchor in the rendered file does the test locate them, so the skill's author and the test share one shape every later edit must keep?

The batched call gets an automated test under both interpreters. Is the compact view's fixed shell call, the list call followed by the walk-fed loop of lift calls, exercised by an automated test too, or does it stay covered by the Claude Code hands-on check alone?
open-question.alternative: No automated test of the compact view call, for good unless a later field run shows it breaking: the call stays covered by the Claude Code hands-on check of the rewritten sweep, and its three tool calls stay covered by the existing per-subcommand suites (test_list.py, test_walk.py, test_lift.py). No new test, fixture, or extraction anchor is added for it, and the batched-call test is the milestone's only template test. The call adds no logic of its own beyond running list, then walk's ids through a read loop into lift, and every one of those prints is already pinned by the tool's tests, so the only untested part is a few lines of shell glue that the hands-on check runs for real, in the user's own shell, at no added test or anchor cost. The call is the sweep's whole gather and order and the read that the field broke most often (33 of 88 runs lost a turn to the zsh separator in today's read), yet a later edit that breaks it, drops the list half, or reorders its print passes CI and surfaces only in a run or in the next hands-on check, which today covers no host's sweep at all.

An automated test of its own in tests/, run in CI under both pytest interpreters, that extracts the compact view call from a rendered host tree, replaces <MILESTONE_DIR> with a golden fixture milestone copied to a temporary directory, runs the call under bash, and asserts its print: every block's id, tab, and question text in document order, recommendation-less blocks included, followed by each walked id and that id's lifted line in walk order. Bash only, matching the batched-call test; no git repository is needed since the call writes nothing. The read the sweep reasons over is pinned on every push, independently of the batched-call test, so a regression in the gather is reported as the gather's failure, and the test is cheap because the call has no per-question placeholder to fill and needs no git setup. Bash is not the shell that broke the field reads (zsh), so the test does not reach the failure class that motivated the compact view, and the failed-lift branch (an Error: line in place of the pick) cannot be provoked from a valid fixture, since walk prints only blocks lift accepts, so that branch stays with the hands-on check. Depends on the extraction anchor the sibling question settles also locating a second fixed call in the same rendered file.

alternative.id: Separate executed test under bash and zsh

open-question.alternative: The same separate executed test as under bash, extracting the call from a rendered host tree, running it on a copied fixture milestone, and asserting the same print, but run once under bash and once under zsh, the zsh run skipping itself where no zsh is installed, in CI under both pytest interpreters. It exercises the call in the shell that broke today's read (the macOS default, where the separator's =cmd expansion failed), so a later edit that reintroduces a zsh-unsafe form fails a test on any maintainer machine that has zsh rather than in a field run. CI's ubuntu-latest runner is not guaranteed to carry zsh, so the zsh leg may run only on maintainer machines and skip silently in CI, adding an environment-keyed skip to a suite whose only skip today is keyed on the interpreter version; the failed-lift branch stays unprovokable from a valid fixture, and it depends on the sibling's extraction anchor also locating a second call.

No separate test: the batched-call test already decided gains a first stage that extracts the compact view call from the same rendered host tree, runs it under bash on the same fixture milestone in its temporary git repository, asserts its print, and fills each batched section's --option value and expected commit body from the lifted lines that print carries rather than from fixture constants, so the two calls are exercised as one run in CI under both pytest interpreters. It covers the hand-off the Option value source decision describes, the runner copying each section's option from the compact view's lifted pick, so a drift between what the compact view prints and what the batched call needs fails one end-to-end test, with one fixture and one harness and no second test file. A compact view regression fails the batched-call test, so a failure no longer says which call broke, and the batched test's correctness now rests on a gather it does not control; it runs under bash only, the failed-lift branch stays unprovokable, and it depends on the sibling's extraction anchor locating both calls in the one rendered file.

alternative.id: Static assertion on the rendered call

open-question.alternative: An automated test in tests/, run in CI under both pytest interpreters, that reads the compact view call from a rendered host tree without running it and asserts its text: list --with-question, walk, and lift each written as the full fixed tool command with no variable, alias, or function standing for it, the loop reading walk's print, and no echo separator between reads. No fixture is copied and no shell runs. It guards exactly the regressions the field and the shell-literal invariant name (a separator, a shortened tool command) at the lowest harness cost of any test, with no fixture, temporary directory, or shell dependency. It checks the file rather than the run, so a call that is textually right but prints the wrong shape or order passes, the field failures came from runners rewriting commands, which no test of the file reaches, and it starts a new kind of test, prose assertions on a rendered skill, that the suite does not hold today; it depends on the sibling's extraction anchor also locating this call.
